original:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $u$ be an integer with $\operatorname{gcd}(u,p)=1$ , and let $k,j$ be positive integers such that $p^{j}\leq k$ . For each integer $z$ , define

 $N_{j}(z)=\#\left\{i\in\mathbb{Z}:0\leq i\leq k,p^{j}\mid z+ui\right\}.$ 

If $p^{j}\mid k+1$ , then $N_{j}(z)=\frac{k+1}{p^{j}}$ for every integer $z$ . Otherwise, $N_{j}(z)$ takes two consecutive integer values and has least positive period $p^{j}$ .
